summary: Light on a small island at the entrance to Hermitage Bay, Newfoundland, first shown in 1879; a Coast Guard station that the 2011 Senate report counts among remote sites.

notes_for_editor: Built from LighthouseFriends (copyrighted: facts paraphrased, no quotation longer than a short phrase), Rowlett, the CCG list and the Senate 2011 appendices. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the LSS stranding tables are by fiscal year (1902 table: fiscal years 1893-1902 plus a Total column), so 'dates' were wrongly described; the story now says the tables give counts by fiscal year. The LSS entry appears in other years' tables too (corpus grep: 1889 to 1906 hits, the 1889 OCR reads 'frermitage Bay'); the story cites only the 1902 and 1907 reports, so no range is claimed. Senate page numbers corrected: automation statements on printed p. 6, remote-site figure p. 7, Appendix 5 Pass Island row p. 43, Appendix 6 p. 45. The Senate's Appendix 5 lists four staffed positions at Pass Island while its text describes all 23 staffed NL stations as automated; the story states both without resolving them. Tower height: CCG 9.4 m (structure height column); Rowlett 9.5 m; both are stated in the story. Rowlett (ibiblio) says the island is accessible only by boat and that station buildings had fallen into ruin by 2008; LighthouseFriends says grounds open. Removed two events that were not station events: the 1902 stranding-table entry and the 1974 community relocation. CCG fog horn: blast 3 s, silence 27 s. The 1879 red light was fixed; the current CCG secondary light is Fl R 4s. Current staffing is unknown; the newest figure is April 2010. Keeper spans are LighthouseFriends' 'at least' dates and were kept as approximate. No photos added.
